texts.li: {X_nameDef} came in with the {FACTION} party three days ago and has spent most of that time at {A_nameDef}'s elbow, hauling with {A_objective}, eating with {A_objective}, laughing at {A_possessive} jokes. Tonight {X_nameDef} asked the council at supper whether there is room for one more.\n\n{FACTION} won't thank anyone for keeping a pair of its hands. {A_nameDef} is studying the floor and trying hard not to look as if the answer matters.

Every evening since the {FACTION} people made camp by the colony, {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} have ended up at the same fire and stayed long after it burned down. Now {X_nameDef} wants to stay when the rest of them move on.\n\nWhoever speaks for the group has made it clear that {X_nameDef} owes them, and that they will remember who kept {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} hasn't asked the council for anything, but it's plain what {A_pronoun} wants.

The {FACTION} visitors leave at first light, and {X_nameDef} would rather not go with them. In two days {X_nameDef} has mended {A_nameDef}'s boots, learned the names of most of the colony's animals, and told the council plainly that nothing back home is worth the walk.\n\n{A_nameDef} says the colony could use the extra hands, though it's clear that isn't the only reason.

li.label: Welcome {X_nameDef} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} unpacked in the colony that night. The rest of the {FACTION} party left at dawn without a word to anyone, and {FACTION} will remember it.

li.label: Pay {FACTION} to let {X_objective} go
li.outcome: The council paid {FACTION} two hundred silver for the trouble, and {X_nameDef} stayed. Some here think that's a lot of silver to pay for one person.

li.label: {X_nameDef} leaves with {X_possessive} people
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} left with {FACTION} at first light. {A_nameDef} found something to fix on the far side of the colony and stayed there all morning.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} left with {FACTION} at first light. {A_nameDef} walked with them a good way down the road, and kept going alone after they had parted.

li.label: Ask our best talker to square it with {FACTION}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with whoever speaks for {FACTION} and talked it through: a debt forgiven here, a promise there. {X_nameDef} stayed, and {FACTION} left on decent terms.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {B_nameDef} shared a pipe with the {FACTION} elders and talked until the fire burned low. {X_nameDef} stayed, and the elders left without hard feelings.
[b:past:trader] {B_nameDef} haggled with {FACTION} as if {X_nameDef} were a bolt of cloth, which seemed to be what they understood. {X_nameDef} stayed, and they parted on decent terms.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} talked with the {FACTION} visitors until dark and got nowhere. {X_nameDef} stayed anyway, and {FACTION} left angry.

texts.li: At dinner {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} looked at {A_nameDef}'s plate, then at {A_nameDef}, and said loudly that back home they feed that to the pigs. Then {X_nameDef} explained what they do with people like {A_nameDef}. Only the other visitors laughed.\n\n{A_nameDef} put down {A_possessive} spoon very slowly, and has asked the council what it intends to do about its guest.

{X_nameDef} has spent the whole visit telling anyone who'll listen what is wrong with {A_nameDef}: the voice, the walk, the smell, the sort of family that produces a person like that. {A_nameDef} has heard every word of it, because {X_nameDef} made sure of it.\n\nThe colony wants to stay on good terms with {FACTION}. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether a guest is allowed to say anything at all.

{X_nameDef} spat on the floor {A_nameDef} swept that morning and called {A_objective} something that made the cook drop a ladle. When {A_nameDef} asked {X_nameDef} to repeat it, {X_nameDef} did, slower.\n\nThe {FACTION} visitors are guests, and guests are supposed to be safe here. {A_nameDef} has asked the council whether that still holds for this one.

li.label: Demand an apology
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} was made to apologize to {A_nameDef} at supper, and managed it without once looking up from {X_possessive} plate. {A_nameDef} was satisfied.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} was told to apologize, laughed in {A_nameDef}'s face, and a minute later the two of them were rolling in the dirt. {FACTION} won't be pleased when it hears.

li.label: Let it go, they're guests
li.outcome: The council said nothing to {X_nameDef}, who took that as encouragement. {A_nameDef} ate the rest of {A_possessive} meals somewhere else until the visitors left.

li.label: Throw the lot of them out
li.outcome: The whole {FACTION} party was told to leave and walked to the gate, {X_nameDef} talking the entire way. {A_nameDef} watched them go with {A_possessive} arms folded.

li.label: Ask our best talker to settle it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} had a quiet word with the {FACTION} visitors, and {X_nameDef} kept to the guests' fire for the rest of the stay. {A_nameDef} was satisfied.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {B_nameDef} went to the {FACTION} elders with a jug of something strong. By evening {X_nameDef} had been told off by {X_possessive} own people, and {A_nameDef} got a gruff nod across the yard.
[b:office:Speaker] The colony's speaker took the {FACTION} visitors aside and spoke for the colony. {X_nameDef} said nothing more to {A_nameDef} for the rest of the stay.

li.riskOutcome: The {FACTION} visitors heard {B_nameDef} out and took {X_nameDef}'s side. They left a day early, and {A_nameDef} is still angry.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, has been turning over the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries, the one that belonged to somebody now buried out back. {X_nameDef} calls it good old work, the kind collectors pay for.\n\nThe offer is real silver, more than the thing is worth to anyone who didn't know its owner. {A_nameDef} hasn't said yes or no, and keeps glancing at the council.

{X_nameDef} noticed the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries within a minute of arriving, and has come back to it four times since, each time with a better offer.\n\nThe colony is short of silver. The heirloom is one of the few things {A_nameDef} has left of the dead, and {A_nameDef} wants the council to decide.

li.label: Sell it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} handed it over and counted the {COUNT} silver twice, then went and sat by the graves until supper.

li.label: Haggle until it hurts
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} haggled until {X_nameDef} was sweating, and got {COUNT} silver for it. The heirloom went into the trader's pack, and {A_nameDef} went off to be alone.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} pushed the price once too often. {X_nameDef} put the heirloom down, said something unkind about frontier manners, and walked off. {A_nameDef} still has it, and is more relieved than {A_pronoun} expected to be.

li.label: It stays with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The heirloom stays with {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} shrugged, said everyone has a price, and seemed to think better of {A_nameDef} for refusing.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} has been talking to {A_nameDef} through the cell door every night, about the people waiting back with {FACTION}, a field that won't plant itself, and how none of this was ever {X_possessive} idea. {A_nameDef} believes every word.\n\nNow {A_nameDef} is asking the council to let {X_nameDef} go home. The ones who caught {X_nameDef} remember things differently.

{A_nameDef} carried {X_nameDef}'s meal down this morning and came back without the bowl and with a request. {X_nameDef} has a child back with {FACTION}, or says so, and begged {A_nameDef} to ask the council for {X_possessive} freedom.\n\nIt might be true. Prisoners say a great many things, and {A_nameDef} has never been good at telling the true ones from the rest.

li.label: Let {X_objective} go home
li.outcome: The wardens have orders to let {X_nameDef} go. {X_nameDef} thanked {A_nameDef} with both hands and swore that {FACTION} would hear how {X_pronoun} was treated here.

li.label: Hear {X_objective} out properly
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat by the cell door for three evenings and listened to all of it. {X_nameDef} has stopped glaring at the wardens, and {A_nameDef} has started saving {X_objective} the better bread.

li.label: Keep the door locked
li.outcome: The door stays locked. {A_nameDef} still carries {X_nameDef}'s meals down, and doesn't stay to talk anymore.

texts.li: The fighting is over, and one of the {FACTION} attackers is still alive in the dirt not far from {A_nameDef}, holding a wound that won't stop bleeding. {X_nameDef} is asking {A_nameDef} for help in a voice that keeps cracking. A few minutes ago {X_nameDef} was trying to kill {A_objective}.\n\n{A_nameDef} is looking to the council, and {X_nameDef} doesn't have long.

{A_nameDef} was walking among the fallen when one of them grabbed {A_possessive} ankle. It was {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, alive and bleeding badly, begging for someone to decide what happens to {X_objective}.\n\nThe choices are a prison bed, a quick blade, or leaving {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} lies. {X_nameDef} is losing blood the whole time the council thinks about it.

li.label: Take {X_objective} prisoner
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went to carry {X_nameDef} to a prison bed, muttering that somebody had better have made one.

li.label: End it quickly
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} knelt beside {X_nameDef}, said something too low for anyone else to hear, and made it quick.

li.label: Leave {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} lies
li.outcome: No one went back for {X_nameDef}. Toward evening the calling stopped.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} caught {A_nameDef} away from the others and asked in a low voice whether the colony could spare any food. The damp got into their stores this season. Their children have been living on bark soup, and the walk home is long.\n\n{X_nameDef} didn't beg, only stood there afterward, waiting for an answer.

{A_nameDef} counted a handful of {FACTION} people at the gate, thin as fence rails, one of them carrying a child too tired to cry. {X_nameDef} speaks for them. They want food, whatever the colony can spare.\n\nThe colony can spare some. The cooks want to know whether it can still spare it come midwinter.

li.label: Fill their sacks
li.outcome: The {FACTION} people left with their sacks full of the colony's food, and {X_nameDef} promised they would remember it. The cooks have started stretching the winter stores to make up the difference.

li.label: Give them silver instead
li.outcome: The council gave {X_nameDef} sixty silver and directions to the nearest market. It's a long walk, but they left in better spirits than they came.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The colony's food stayed in the colony's storeroom. The {FACTION} people waited until dusk, then walked on, slower than they came.

li.label: Send them home with seed, and a grower's advice
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon with {X_nameDef} going over what grows where and when, and sent {X_objective} home with a sack of food and a pouch of seed. {FACTION} should eat better next year.

outcomes.li: [winter] {B_nameDef} sent {X_nameDef} home with enough food to get through the cold and a pouch of seed for the thaw, and drew {X_objective} a map of where to plant it.
[b:past:farmer] {B_nameDef} grew up on a farm and talked {X_nameDef} through it the way {B_possessive} own parents would have: soil, water, rotation. {FACTION} went home with seed and a sack of food.

texts.li: This afternoon {PET_nameDef} bit {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, hard enough to draw blood. {X_nameDef} says it came out of nowhere. {A_nameDef}, whose animal it is, says {X_nameDef} tried to take something out of {PET_possessive} mouth.\n\n{FACTION} would like compensation. {A_nameDef} would like the council to remember whose side it's on.

{X_nameDef} is showing everyone the teeth marks in {X_possessive} hand. They're from {PET_definite}, {A_nameDef}'s animal, and {A_nameDef} says anyone who pats a sleeping animal on the head gets what's coming.\n\nThe {FACTION} visitors want silver for the bite. One or two of them want {PET_definite} as well.

li.label: Pay for the bite
li.outcome: The council paid {X_nameDef} eighty silver for the bite. {X_nameDef} counted it with the bandaged hand, which no longer seemed to hurt.

li.label: Stand by {PET_definite}
li.outcome: The council ruled that guests should keep their hands off other people's animals. {FACTION} took that badly, and {A_nameDef} gave {PET_definite} an extra helping at dinner.

li.label: Hand {PET_definite} over to them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} led {PET_definite} away on a rope, rubbing the bite. {A_nameDef} watched them all the way to the tree line and is not speaking to the council.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came back from work pale: {X_indefinite} has made a den close to the colony and has been watching the paths. It hasn't attacked anyone yet, but it killed something large last night, and {A_nameDef} found what was left.\n\n{B_nameDef}, who handles the colony's animals, wants to try taming it. Others want it dead before it decides people are food.

{A_nameDef} nearly stepped on {X_indefinite} sleeping in the brush near the colony. Its tracks go right past the storeroom, and twice now it has followed the haulers home, keeping a careful distance.\n\nThe council can send hunters, send {B_nameDef} out with a bucket of food, or hope it gets bored and wanders off.

li.label: Hunt it
li.outcome: The council marked {X_definite} for the hunters. {B_nameDef} called it a waste of a fine animal, and was overruled.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} try to tame it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} has been put in charge of taming {X_definite}, and the others have been told to stay well back from the den.

li.label: Leave it alone
li.outcome: The council left {X_definite} to its own business. So far it has kept to its den, and the haulers have started carrying sticks.
li.riskOutcome: The council left {X_definite} alone, and for two days it returned the favor. On the third it came out of the brush at a dead run, straight for the nearest person.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been feeding {X_indefinite} behind the storeroom for a week, out of {A_possessive} own dinner, and has given it a name no one else is allowed to say. Today {A_nameDef} came to the council with a speech that had clearly been practiced. It's very clean, it's very quiet, and {A_nameDef} promises to do all the work.\n\nThe adults suspect the feeding and cleaning will end up with the handlers.

There is {X_indefinite} following {A_nameDef} around the colony at a careful distance. {A_nameDef} swears it came on its own, though the trail of berries says otherwise.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to keep it. It's another mouth, it's wild, and it will chew something important. {A_nameDef} has heard all of that and is still standing there.

li.label: Let {A_objective} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a pet now, and has introduced it to every person in the colony. It sleeps at the foot of {A_possessive} bed.

li.label: Let the handlers try, properly
li.outcome: The council put {X_definite} on the handlers' list. {A_nameDef} has been following the handlers around ever since, giving advice.

li.label: No, and that's final
li.outcome: The answer was no. {A_nameDef} has been sulking, loudly, in whichever room the council happens to be in.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} was told no, and went missing for half a day. Someone finally found {A_objective} out past the fields, sitting next to {X_definite}, not speaking to anyone.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the titled guest, inspected the room {A_nameDef} built, ran a finger along the wall, and asked whether the colony keeps pigs in it the rest of the year. {A_nameDef} spent days on that room.\n\n{X_nameDef}'s patrons will hear how {X_nameDef} was treated here. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether the council will stand up for the work.

Over supper {X_nameDef} explained to the whole table that the servants' quarters back home are better built than the finest room in this colony, and looked straight at {A_nameDef} while saying it. {A_nameDef} raised most of the walls in the place.\n\nNo one has answered yet. {A_nameDef}, hammer still in hand, has asked the council whether a title means you get to say that.

li.label: Say nothing and smile
li.outcome: No one contradicted {X_nameDef}, who took the silence as agreement and enjoyed the rest of the evening. {A_nameDef} spent the next day hammering at the workbench, harder than the work needed.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} answer back
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} exactly what a title is worth out here. {X_nameDef} left the table, and {FACTION} will hear about it.

li.label: Ask what would please {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} asked {X_nameDef}, politely, what a proper room would look like. The answer took all afternoon, and since then {A_nameDef} has been looking at the colony's rooms with a far more critical eye.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, has a small green bottle and a loud voice. The tonic inside cures aching joints, bad dreams, low spirits and baldness, {X_nameDef} says, and makes the old feel thirty again. It's the last bottle, and it costs one hundred silver.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been suffering from most of those things lately, and can't stop looking at it.

{A_nameDef} hasn't slept properly in weeks, and {X_nameDef} the trader spotted it right away. Now there's a stoppered bottle on the table between them, and {X_nameDef} is explaining that it was brewed by hermits from a root that only grows on graves.\n\nIt costs one hundred silver. {A_nameDef} wants it, and the council holds the purse.

li.label: Buy {A_objective} the tonic
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} drank the tonic in one swallow, pulled a terrible face, and slept fourteen hours straight. {A_nameDef} woke up feeling better than {A_pronoun} has in weeks.
li.riskOutcome: The tonic was water, sugar and something that tasted like an old boot. {A_nameDef} drank all of it anyway, out of spite, and people have been calling {A_objective} the alchemist since.

li.label: Make {X_nameDef} drink some first
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took a swig, smacked {X_possessive} lips, and fell asleep on {X_possessive} own pack. When {X_nameDef} woke up, the council bought the rest for sixty silver.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} suddenly decided the tonic was far too precious for a trader to drink, packed it away in a huff, and wouldn't sell it after that.

li.label: Keep the silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} put the bottle away with a sigh and told {A_nameDef} it might still be there next time. {A_nameDef} keeps wondering whether it would have worked.

li.label: Have our doctor mix a sleeping draught
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} mixed {A_nameDef} a sleeping draught from the colony's own medicine. It tasted no better than the tonic would have, and {A_nameDef} slept until noon.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} boiled up a draught of herbs from the colony's own stores, bitter as bark. {A_nameDef} drank it, grimaced, and slept through to noon.
[b:past:healer] {B_nameDef} has treated a hundred bad sleepers and knew what to give. {A_nameDef} slept until noon, and {X_nameDef} put the tonic away with a sour look.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} came in with the {FACTION} party and recognized {A_nameDef} across the yard. They knew each other before, somewhere else, when {A_nameDef} was living a different life, and {X_nameDef} knows all about it ({SECRET}).\n\n{X_nameDef} has been very friendly about it, and has mentioned that keeping quiet is a kind of work, and work should be paid. One hundred and fifty silver ought to cover it.

{A_nameDef} went white when {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walked in, and has been finding reasons to be elsewhere ever since. Tonight {A_nameDef} came to the council in private. {X_nameDef} knew {A_objective} before the colony, and knows something no one here does ({SECRET}).\n\n{X_nameDef} wants one hundred and fifty silver to keep it that way. {A_nameDef} can't pay that. The colony can.

li.label: Pay for {X_possessive} silence
li.outcome: The silver changed hands behind the storeroom. {X_nameDef} went back to the other visitors whistling, and {A_nameDef} finally got a decent night's sleep.
li.riskOutcome: The council paid {X_nameDef} a hundred and fifty silver to keep quiet. By the next evening, {X_nameDef} had told the story over supper anyway.

li.label: Let {X_objective} talk
li.outcome: The council refused to pay. {X_nameDef} shrugged and told the whole dining room over dinner, including details {A_nameDef} had managed to forget.

li.label: Threaten {X_objective}
li.outcome: A few of the colony's bigger people had a word with {X_nameDef} behind the storeroom. {X_nameDef} has kept the secret since, and doesn't say much to anyone.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} explained to {X_nameDef} why talking would be unwise. {X_nameDef} told everyone anyway, at the top of {X_possessive} voice, and a moment later the two of them were trading blows across the dining table.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the beast at the tree line

texts.li: {A_nameDef} saw it at the tree line this morning: {X_definite}, the beast that mauled one of the colonists and limped off into the wild. It's back, pacing past the fields as if waiting for a door to be left open.\n\nThe colony wants it dealt with, but people can't agree whether that means hunting it, taming it, or staying indoors until it loses interest.

There are tracks around the colony again, deep ones, and {A_nameDef} knows whose they are. They belong to {X_definite}, the animal that tore into a colonist, got away, and earned itself a name.\n\nSome want it dead today. Some want it tamed, which doesn't sit well with the one it mauled. They all want the council to decide soon.

li.label: Hunt it down now
li.outcome: The council marked {X_definite} for death, and {A_nameDef} was the first to pick up a weapon. The others are staying indoors until it's done.

li.label: Keep everyone inside
li.outcome: Everyone stays indoors until {X_definite} wanders off. The work is piling up, and people are getting on each other's nerves.

li.label: Try to tame it
li.outcome: The council marked {X_definite} for taming. If the handlers manage it, the colony will have the fiercest animal for miles around, and plenty of people are nervous about the attempt.
li.riskOutcome: The council marked {X_definite} for taming. The first handler got halfway across the clearing before it charged. Now it's loose among the buildings, hunting people.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} is the one who hurt {A_nameDef} and got away. Now {X_nameDef} sits in a cell, eating the colony's food and sleeping under the colony's roof, and {A_nameDef} has stood outside that door every night since the capture, saying nothing.\n\nThe council has to decide what {X_nameDef} is now: a debt to be settled, a mouth to be fed, or a pair of hands to be won over.

{A_nameDef} still carries what {X_nameDef} did, in the body and elsewhere. {X_nameDef} still has the nerve to ask the wardens for an extra blanket.\n\nThe colony wants to know what the council means to do with this prisoner. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether {A_possessive} say counts for anything.

li.label: Execute {X_objective}
li.outcome: The wardens have their orders. {A_nameDef} asked to be there when it happens, and the council agreed.

li.label: Let {X_objective} rot in there
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stays in the cell, fed and ignored. {A_nameDef} no longer goes near that end of the colony.

li.label: Try to recruit {X_objective}
li.outcome: The wardens have started trying to win {X_nameDef} over. {A_nameDef} feels betrayed, and so do {A_possessive} friends.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has fallen hard for {PET_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s animal, and has offered one hundred and twenty silver on the spot. With the storeroom as bare as it is, that's a very good price.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been standing between {X_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef} ever since.

Every time the {FACTION} visitors pass {PET_nameDef}, {X_nameDef} stops to scratch an ear and mutters about money. Today {X_nameDef} made a real offer: one hundred and twenty silver, right now, and {PET_nameDef} goes home with {X_nameDef}.\n\nThe colony could use the silver. Some say {PET_nameDef} would be safer somewhere that gets raided less. {A_nameDef} hasn't said a word, but hasn't let go of the lead either.

li.label: Sell {PET_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counted out the silver and led {PET_definite} off on a rope. On the way out {PET_definite} looked back twice, and {A_nameDef} watched until they were out of sight.

li.label: Name a price {X_nameDef} won't pay
li.outcome: The council asked two hundred and fifty silver, expecting a no. {X_nameDef} paid on the spot without haggling, and the animal went home with {X_objective}.
li.riskOutcome: The council asked two hundred and fifty silver. {X_nameDef} called it robbery and went back to {X_possessive} people empty-handed, as the council had hoped.

li.label: Not for sale
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} gave {PET_definite} one last scratch behind the ears and went back to {X_possessive} people. {A_nameDef} hasn't let {PET_objective} out of sight since.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} travels with the {FACTION} party and carries a bag of dried roots and bone needles. {X_nameDef} took one look at the way {A_nameDef} moves and offered to see to the old injury, for eighty silver.\n\n{B_nameDef}, who does most of the colony's doctoring, wants to watch and learn, though {B_pronoun} suspects half of what's in that bag is dirt.

Word got around that {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, is a healer. {A_nameDef}, who has been favoring an old injury for as long as anyone can remember, went to ask and came back with a price. For eighty silver, {X_nameDef} will see what can be done.\n\n{B_nameDef} has offered to assist, mostly to keep an eye on what goes into {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Pay the healer
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} worked on {A_nameDef} with hot stones and strong hands for most of the afternoon while {B_nameDef} watched every move. The old injury still aches, but less, and {A_nameDef} is grateful.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} rubbed something brown into {A_nameDef}'s old injury, hummed over it a while, and was gone with the silver before supper. {B_nameDef} learned a few things not to do.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} to teach {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: For sixty silver {X_nameDef} spent the afternoon teaching {B_nameDef} what everything in the bag is for, using {A_nameDef}'s old injury for practice. {A_nameDef} was poked a great deal and helped not at all.

li.label: Keep the silver
li.outcome: The council kept its silver. {X_nameDef} went back to the {FACTION} camp, and {A_nameDef} went on favoring the old injury, making sure the council saw it.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} treat it, with our own medicine
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} worked on {A_nameDef}'s old injury all afternoon with the colony's own medicine, while {X_nameDef} watched and offered advice nobody asked for. It aches less now.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} made a poultice from the colony's herbs and bound {A_nameDef}'s old injury in clean linen. {X_nameDef} looked at the work and said it would do.
